title: Monthly strategy accelerator — executive sync packet & decision lanes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: produce a concise executive-facing packet that surfaces current roadmap health, two tradeable investment lanes, and a prioritized decision register for March exec sync. The packet should enable the SLT to: 1) agree which initiative(s) to accelerate vs. de-scope for Q2 runway, 2) sanction a small budget reallocation (up to 15%) toward Dedicated autoscale improvements if risk profile is accepted, and 3) approve a 3-week canary cadence for a low-risk runtime change.

Scope: cross-functional synthesis across Product, Eng (runtime & infra), Research, and DevRel. Focus pillars: performance economics (cost per token vs. latency curves), reliability SLO delta, and GTM readiness for Dedicated/Private features. Outside scope: deep engineering design docs (these are linked as artifacts).

Expected outputs: single-slide executive summary, 6-slide packet, decision register with owners and deadlines, risk heatmap, and suggested contingency lanes. Packet will live in Confluence and a short deck in Drive for the live sync.
deliverables: Decision register with owners and target gates
Risk heatmap and cost/latency delta table
Follow-up Linear tickets created for approved lanes
blockers: Finalized runtime cost delta numbers from Eng (waiting on perf matrix from ENG-1842)
Legal confirmation for Dedicated contract amendment language if budget reallocation chosen
Missing SLO burn chart for last 30 days (product telemetry refresh in progress)
decisions_sought: Approve lane A (prioritize Dedicated autoscale + caching) with up-to-15% reallocation
Approve lane B (maintain current runway; invest in Optimize tooling) as conservative default
Sign-off on canary cadence for runtime-1.18 micro-ops (3 weeks with automatic rollback thresholds)

notes: Trade-offs discussed: accelerating Dedicated autoscale buys predictable throughput but risks engineering time and a temporary latency bump; Optimize path reduces OPEX over longer horizon but delays immediate throughput gains.
We should prepare a succinct appendix with technical indicators (SLO burn, median/95th latency, tail latencies by model family) for any SLT member who asks for depth.
If execs ask for a single recommendation, default to lane A with strict rollback and a 3-week trial to measure real customer impact.
